steps.title: Borrowed buying power
steps.text:
**Leverage** lets you open a position bigger than your deposit. At **30:1**, $1,000 of **margin** controls a $30,000 position.

Profits and losses are based on the **full $30,000**, not on your $1,000.

steps.title: It cuts both ways
steps.text:
A 1% move against a 30:1 position costs **30%** of the margin you put up.

Leverage doesn't change how much the market moves. It changes how much each move helps, or hurts, you.

steps.question: You open a $20,000 position using $1,000 of margin. The market moves 2% against you. How much do you lose?
steps.explanation: 2% of the **full position**: 2% of $20,000 = **$400**. That's 40% of your margin.

steps.title: Margin calls and close-outs
steps.text:
Your broker needs a minimum amount of margin to keep positions open. If losses eat into it, you may get a **margin call**.

Under EU and UK rules for retail CFD traders, positions are closed automatically when your equity falls to **50%** of the required margin, and you can't lose more than the money in your account (**negative balance protection**).

steps.title: Limits for everyday traders
steps.text:
**EU and UK** retail leverage limits: **30:1** major currency pairs; **20:1** other currency pairs, gold and major indices; **10:1** other commodities and minor indices; **5:1** individual shares; **2:1** crypto.

**US**: retail forex is limited to **50:1** on major pairs and **20:1** on others, and CFDs aren't offered to retail clients.

steps.question: What's the safest way to think about leverage?
options: Use the maximum available to grow faster
Size every trade from your stop and risk %, and treat leverage only as a limit
Leverage affects profits but not losses
steps.explanation: With proper sizing, your risk is set by your stop and your risk %. Leverage only needs to be high enough to allow that size.

points: Leverage = a **big position** from a **small deposit**.
Gains and losses are on the **full** position size.
EU/UK retail: close-out at **50%** margin, and you can't lose more than your account.
Size from your **stop and risk %**; leverage is just a limit.
